To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Galactitol is a substrate for the PEP-dependent phosphotransferases system in E. coli.

galactitol is transported via a specific enzyme II-complex of the PEP-dependent phosphotransfer system and that galactitol dissimilates to dihydroxyaceton- and glyceraldehyde-P via the following pathway: galactitol-6-P-D-Tagatose-6-phosphate-D-tagatose1,6-P- dihydroxyaceton- and glyceraldebyde-P.
the galactitol dissimilatory pathway in E. coli is controlled by the genetic map loci gat, pfkA,pfkB-1, kba and fda.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the dissimilation mechanism of the polyol galactitol (or dulcitol) in E. coli, a process which has been known for a long time but has not been investigated in detail.
the genetic control of the dissimilation and assimilation of galactose and its derivatives in E. coli and S. typhimurium.

the analysis of mutations affecting the transport and metabolism of the sugar alcohols dulcitol and sorbitol, the latter being the most abundant sugar alcohol in the world (about 1% of all carbohydrates in plants).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

galactitol dissimilatory metabolism in E. coli consists of a galactitol permease and a dehydrogenase, both of which are under the control of the gat operons and the phosphofructo-kinase system, and of a temperature sensitive aldolase which is controlled by the gene kba.
the gat locus is an operon, made of three genes, gatA (gat), gatD (gat) and gatC (gat).

galactitol is dissimilated in E. coli via a phosphoenol pyruvate dependent galactitol transport system, catalyzed by the enzymes II-complexGatl and the dehydrogense, and a galactitol dissimilating aldolase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
galactitol dissimilatory enzymes of E. coli are controlled by a new genetic locus kba in addition to the previously reported loci gat, fda and pfk.
the dissimilation and the transport of galactitol are controlled by a gat operone, the phosphofructo-kinases by pfkA and pfkB and a temperature sensitive ketohexose-bis-phosphatase by kba.

the galactitol dissimilating system in E. coli is a typical PTS system, but the PTS enzyme II-complex catalyzes the formation of a phosphorylated intermediate which has to be dephosphorylated by an enzyme not belonging to the PTS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the galactitol pathway is a complex one, and the genes involved are not clustered in the genome.
the dissimilation pathways of galactitol and fructose in E. coli seem to be very similar.
galactitol dissimilatory enzymes in E. coli can be used to produce D-tagatose, a rare ketohexose, from cheap and abundant galactitol.
